evidence: Plaut. Mil. 2.3.51: Quid jam? — Quia luscitiōsus. (Lewis & Short s.v. luscitiōsus)
terms.comment: In Plautus it asks for a reason and is answered with quia. Traupman 111 glosses it “what (is the trouble) now?”, which it does not mean (see what’s the matter?).

terms.grammar: quī, the old ablative “how?”, with istuc
terms.comment: Plautus has quī istuc potis est fierī? (Plaut. Amph. 2.2.62, Lewis & Short s.v. enim); the short form is Traupman’s.

terms.gloss: how come? how does it happen (that …)?
terms.grammar: quī, the old ablative “how”, with fit; a clause with ut follows when the thing is named
evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.1: Quī fit, Maecēnās, ut nēmō … (Lewis & Short s.v. sors)
